ember_india_yearly.name: Ember - India electricity data (subnational, yearly, long format)
ember_india_yearly.coverage: 36 states/UTs, 2019-2024 yearly (monthly file runs to Nov-2025)

cea_co2_baseline_v21.name: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, User Guide v21.0 (FY2024-25)
cea_co2_baseline_v21.value: All-India weighted average 0.710 tCO2/MWh (direct CO2, net generation, incl. RE & captive injection, adjusted for cross-border transfers); OM 0.961, BM 0.512, CM 0.736
cea_co2_baseline_v21.use: cross-check / consumption-side proxy for any Indian location (single national grid)

ember_india_total_2024.basis: lifecycle (IPCC AR5 median factors, gCO2e/kWh), generation-based, utility generation only (excludes captive)

india.basis_statement: All India state values are GENERATION-based (what is generated inside the state's borders), not consumption-based. Indian states trade heavily over one synchronous national grid; for modelling electricity USE, the national CEA factor (~710 g direct) or the Ember India total (621 g lifecycle) is often a better proxy for importing/hydro states.

ci.basis: lifecycle (IPCC AR5 median factors, gCO2e/kWh), generation-based, utility generation only (excludes captive)

caveats: Basis mismatch across countries: India CI is LIFECYCLE (Ember, IPCC AR5 factors, gCO2e); Australia CI is DIRECT combustion (OpenElectricity / NGA). Lifecycle adds roughly 5-15% for gas-heavy grids; do not mix without adjustment.

Ember's IPCC median coal factor (820 g lifecycle) understates Indian coal: CEA's measured direct all-India average is 710 g incl. RE for FY2024-25 vs Ember India total 621 g lifecycle for CY2024. Indian coal-state values are likely ~15-25% low vs plant-specific direct emissions.

India state values are generation-based. Hydro states (HP, J&K, Sikkim, Arunachal, NE states, Kerala, Uttarakhand) show ~24 g but consume coal-heavy grid power; small UTs (Chandigarh, DNH&DD, Goa, Lakshadweep, Delhi) generate little and import most. For modelling consumption, prefer the national factor for such states.
India time span limited to 2019-2024 (Ember subnational series start). India decline rates are 5-year CAGRs and include COVID-2020 and hydrology effects; the national CI was flat (619 -> 621).
Ember India data excludes captive (industrial self-) generation, which is large in India and mostly coal.
Australia: OpenElectricity static v3 endpoint is frozen at Nov-2024, so latest full year is 2023. Newer data requires the authenticated OpenElectricity API.

Australia generation-based CI includes rooftop solar (zero-emission) in the denominator; NGA Scope 2 factors exclude rooftop and include interconnector imports, hence higher (e.g. SA 143 vs 220, TAS 4 vs 200).
Tasmania: generation-based CI (~4 g in 2023) badly understates consumption carbon because of Basslink imports; dec left null.
NT: only a single NGA factor (secondary-sourced) available; fos and dec null.
NGA 2025 factors were read from two agreeing secondary sites, not the DCCEEW primary document (which timed out).
